references.text: God's promise to Abraham that his offspring would be as numerous as the dust of the earth, impossible to count - this is the background for Balaam's statement about Jacob's countless people.
The promise that Abraham's offspring would become as numerous as the stars and the sand, fulfilled in Israel's great number.
God's promise to Jacob that his offspring would be like the dust of the earth - a direct parallel to 'the dust of Jacob'.
The call to consider the blameless and look at the upright, for the man of peace has a future - a parallel to the wish to die the death of the upright and share their end.
The death of the godly is precious in the Lord's sight - connected to the desire to die as the righteous do.
The righteous have refuge even in their death - a parallel to the hope for the end of the righteous.
Blessed are the dead who die in the Lord - a New Testament parallel to the wish to die the death of the upright.
